'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[Australian Government|Australian]] [[Minister for Defence (Australia)|Minister for Defence]] [[Peter Dutton]] says that the country has ended [[Australian Defence Force|its military]] involvement in [[Afghanistan]]. [https://www.voanews.com/south-central-asia/australia-says-last-troops-withdrawn-afghanistan?amp (VOA)]
*[[Assassination of Jovenel Moïse]]
**Suspects in the [[assassination]] of [[President of Haiti|Haitian President]] [[Jovenel Moïse]] say that their intent was to arrest, not kill, Moïse. The two [[Haitian-American]] suspects say that they were working as translators for the [[Colombians|Colombian]] suspects and that they had an arrest warrant against Moïse, but found him dead when they arrived. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/haiti-suspects-say-they-meant-arrest-not-kill-president-report-2021-07-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Twelve people are killed and 26 others injured when a minibus carrying [[illegal immigrant]]s from [[Afghanistan]], [[Pakistan]] and [[Bangladesh]] crashes and catches fire in [[Muradiye]], [[Van Province]], [[Turkey]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/11/at-least-12-killed-as-bus-carrying-migrants-crashes-in-turkey (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record 11,874 new cases and 230 deaths from [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 1.02 million and the nationwide death toll to 16,419. [https://bdnews24.com/coronavirus-pandemic/2021/07/11/bangladesh-logs-230-virus-deaths-11874-cases-in-a-day-grim-records-in-both (Bdnews24.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cambodia]]
****[[Cambodia]] surpasses 60,000 cases of COVID-19. [https://www.khmertimeskh.com/50891593/cambodia-passes-60000-case-mark-as-high-cases-deaths-and-imported-cases-continue/ (''Khmer Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Indonesia]]
*****Indonesia receives three million doses of the [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine]] from the [[United States]], facilitated through the [[COVAX]] initiative. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5639215/kabar-baik-3-juta-lebih-dosis-vaksin-moderna-tiba-di-ri (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Israel]]
*****The [[Ministry of Health (Israel)|Ministry of Health]] announces that [[Israel]] will resume administering first doses of the [[Pfizer COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/with-new-pfizer-deal-israel-to-restart-vaccinations-after-24-hour-break/ (''Times of Israel'')]
*****[[Prime Minister of Israel|Israeli Prime Minister]] [[Naftali Bennett]] announces that a deal has been reached with [[Pfizer]] [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] [[Albert Bourla]], which would see a new shipment of [[vaccine]]s delivered on August 1. [https://www.jpost.com/breaking-news/coronavirus-in-israel-immunocompromised-can-get-jab-today-health-min-673464 (''Jerusalem Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record 1,953 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 29,816. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/se-asia/vietnam-to-expand-movement-curbs-as-covid-19-cases-hit-record-high (''The Straits Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Africa]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Libya]]
****[[Libya]] reports a record 2,854 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 204,090. [http://alwasat.ly/news/libya/326192 (Al-Wasat)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
****[[President of South Africa|President]] [[Cyril Ramaphosa]] extends [[South Africa]]'s level four restrictions for 14 days until July 25 amid a third wave of COVID-19 caused by the [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://businesstech.co.za/news/government/505036/ramaphosa-extends-level-4-lockdown-for-south-africa-here-are-the-new-restrictions/amp/ (Business Tech)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
****[[New South Wales]] reports [[Australia]]'s first death from COVID-19 in 10 months after a woman in her 90s died in [[Sydney]] after contracting the virus in a family setting. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-57793539 (BBC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] surpasses 10,000 cases of COVID-19 after reporting 485 new cases and three deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. The country has seen a significant increase in the number of infections since an outbreak in April. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/446669/fiji-covid-19-485-new-cases-and-three-more-deaths (RNZ)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Peru]]
***Interim [[President of Peru|President]] [[Francisco Sagasti]] extends the COVID-19 [[state of emergency]] in [[Peru]] until the end of August. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/11/peru-extends-covid-state-of-emergency-until-end-of-august (Al Jazeera)]
*Authorities in [[Spain]] issue a [[heat wave]] warning for [[Madrid]] and the southern city of [[Seville]] for the second consecutive day as temperatures reach {{convert|44|C|F}}. [https://www.france24.com/en/europe/20210711-spain-hit-by-heatwave-with-temperatures-set-to-top-44%C2%BAc (France 24)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Oman–Saudi Arabia relations]]
**In his first official overseas trip since assuming power last year, [[House of Al Said|Omani Sultan]] [[Haitham bin Tariq]] meets with [[House of Saud|King]] [[Salman of Saudi Arabia]] in [[Neom]] for two days to discuss a [[Yemeni peace process|peace initiative in Yemen]], and strengthen economic and investment agreements between [[Saudi Arabia]] and [[Oman]]. Saudi media reports it is also Salman's first face-to-face meeting with a world leader since the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia|COVID-19 pandemic]] began. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/11/omans-sultan-visits-saudi-arabia-on-first-overseas-trip (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[LGBT rights in Georgia (country)]], [[2021 attack on Tbilisi Pride]]
**Police in [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]] open a criminal investigation into the death of a journalist who was assaulted during attacks targeting [[LGBT]]+ activists planning the [[Tbilisi]] [[pride march]]. Organizers eventually called off the march when more homophobic attacks took place. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/georgia-probes-death-journalist-beaten-during-attacks-lgbt-supporters-2021-07-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[July 2021 Bulgarian parliamentary election]]
**[[Bulgaria]] holds another election after the three largest parties failed to form a coalition government following the [[April 2021 Bulgarian parliamentary election|election in April]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/05/05/bulgaria-to-hold-fresh-parliamentary-elections-in-july-after-coalition-talks-fail (Euronews)]
**Exit polls do not show a clear winner, with newly-formed populist party [[There Is Such a People]] narrowly beating out [[GERB]], the party of previous Prime Minister [[Boyko Borisov]], by 0.2 percentage points. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/bulgarians-vote-second-national-election-3-months-amid-anger-over-graft-2021-07-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Moldovan parliamentary election]]
**Moldovan voters head to the polls in a snap election to elect new members of the [[Parliament of the Republic of Moldova|Parliament]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/11/polls-open-in-moldovas-snap-election-amid-corruption-concerns (Al Jazeera)]
**Results show the pro-[[European Union|EU]] [[Party of Action and Solidarity]], which [[President of Moldova|President]] [[Maia Sandu]] has close ties to, as the winner with 52% of the vote. [https://www.dw.com/en/moldova-election-pro-eu-party-leads-in-early-results/a-58228907 (DW)]
*[[2021 Cuban protests]]
**Thousands of [[Cubans]], most of them young, attend a rare anti-[[government of Cuba|governmen]]t protest in [[San Antonio de los Baños]] to protest the increased food and medicine shortages brought on by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Cuba|COVID-19 pandemic]]. Hundreds of [[Cuban Americans|Cubans]] in [[Miami]], [[Florida]], United States, hold solidarity protests as [[Mayor of Miami|Mayor]] [[Francis Suarez]] calls for an international intervention against the Cuban government in a [[press conference]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210711-thousands-join-rare-anti-government-protests-in-cuba (France 24)] [https://www.nbcmiami.com/news/hundreds-of-protesters-take-to-miami-streets-as-mayor-asks-for-u-s-led-intervention-in-cuba/2492603/ (NBC Miami)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Virgin Galactic Unity 22]]
**British billionaire [[Richard Branson]] travels into space aboard the [[VSS Unity|VSS ''Unity'']], a [[spaceplane]] owned and operated by the [[space flight]] company [[Virgin Galactic]]. At the age of 70, he is the second oldest person to travel to [[outer space]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/science-environment-57798167/ (BBC News)]

'''Sports'''
*[[UEFA Euro 2020]]
**[[UEFA Euro 2020 Final]]
***[[Italy national football team|Italy]] beats [[England national football team|England]] 3–2 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]] in the UEFA Euro 2020 Final after a 1–1 draw following [[extra time]]. [https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/51198762 (BBC Sport)]
***[[England]] fans storm [[London]]'s [[Wembley Stadium]] ahead of the team's matchup against [[Italy]], with many of the intruders not removed from the stadium until halfway through the match. [https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/kings-cross-station-closed-as-england-fans-set-off-flares-kc7jqkkt5 (''The Times'')]
